Marketing design system

Every token and component of schedulink.io, drawn from the same files the site builds from. Generated; light only.

Brand

Logo

The official files. Never redrawn, recoloured or cropped. See docs/02-brand.md.

Color

The brand ramp

Twelve steps generated from one colour, #2A5BD7. Step 9 is the input itself. White on it: 5.87:1. Brand text (step 11) reaches 7.05:1 on its worst ground.

1#FCFDFFApp background
2#F6F9FFSubtle background
3#EBF2FFElement tint
4#E1EBFFHovered tint
5#D1E0FFSelected tint
6#BDD2FESubtle border
7#A3C1FDBorder
8#81A7F8Strong border
9#2A5BD7Solid
10#1A48C2Pressed solid
11#1E48B5Brand text
12#09205ADarkest

Color

Roles

The names components use. Brand roles follow the ramp; the rest are set by hand.

surface#FFFFFF

Default page background. Most of the site sits on this.

surface-sunken#F7F7F8

Alternating section bands. Never two sunken bands in a row.

surface-raised#FFFFFF

Cards and panels. On light they need a line border to read, since there are no shadows.

surface-invert#2F2F2F

Reserved. The footer sits on the grey, not on a dark band (Seenu, 2026-10-27), so nothing on the site uses this yet.

ink#2F2F2F

The house dark. Headlines and primary text.

ink-secondary#46484C

Body copy and supporting paragraphs.

ink-muted#4D4F53

Eyebrow labels, captions, metadata. Never body copy.

brand#2A5BD7brand.9

The ScheduLink blue, from the logo. Buttons, links, active states and the mark itself. Nothing decorative.

brand-strong#1E48B5brand.11 · was #1F43A8

Link text on light grounds and primary button hover.

brand-soft#EBF2FFbrand.3 · was #ECEFFA

Tint behind a positive status chip or an active nav item. Text on it is brand-strong.

on-brand#FFFFFF

Text and icons on brand fills.

attention#EFEFF1

Ground for anything that needs attention: a conflict flag, an overdue chip, a roster still outstanding. Neutral by design, with ink text and a 3px ink rule carrying the emphasis instead of a colour.

line#E6E6E8

Hairline borders, section rules, table dividers. Structure comes from these, not from shadows.

line-strong#8A8C91

Input and control borders, secondary button outlines, focus rings.

page-grey#F3F3F4

The page ground. Sections float on it as white cards.

status-overdue-bg#FDE8E8

Overdue status pill background.

status-overdue-text#941C13

Overdue status pill text.

status-today-bg#F2ECFC

Due-today status pill background. Purple is used for due-today only.

status-today-text#58339F

Due-today status pill text.

status-later-bg#EBF2FFbrand.3 · was #EEF2FC

Due-later status pill background.

status-later-text#1E48B5brand.11 · was #1F43A8

Due-later status pill text.

illus-rim#F3F3F5

Soft rim around product illustrations.

illus-rim-line#E6E6E9

Border of the soft rim.

illus-header-rule#DCDDE1

Line under column headers in product illustrations.

illus-placeholder#ECECF0

Placeholder lines and pills in simplified rows.

illus-shootcard#F6F9FFbrand.2 · was #F4F6FB

Shoot card background in the Photographers column.

illus-shootcard-line#E1EBFFbrand.4 · was #E6EBF6

Shoot card border.

illus-tile-line#E1EBFFbrand.4 · was #DBE4FA

Border of the pale blue column-header tile in product illustrations. The tile itself is brand-soft.

illus-date#EBF2FFbrand.3

Date tile and part tile fill in tab pictures.

illus-date-line#D1E0FFbrand.5

Border of the date tile in tab pictures.

symbol-line#E3E3E7

Border of the white tile behind a benefit symbol.

confirm#2C9A4B

The green tick badge on a benefit symbol. Shapes only, always with a tick, never text.

grid-line#EBEBEE

Lines of the background grid behind homepage sections (Seenu, 2026-10-20).

grid-node#B3B5B9

Dots where background grid lines meet.

grid-mark#9FA1A6

Corner cross marks on section edges.

Layout

Spacing

space-1 · 4px

Gap between a marker dot and its label.

space-2 · 8px

Inside chips and between stacked list items.

space-3 · 12px

Button padding, gap between a heading and its eyebrow.

space-4 · 16px

Gap between a heading and its paragraph.

space-5 · 24px

Card padding and grid gutters on mobile.

space-6 · 32px

Card padding on desktop, gap between cards.

space-7 · 48px

Gap between a section header and its content.

space-8 · 80px

Section padding, top and bottom, on desktop and phones (Seenu, 2026-10-20: each section fits one laptop screen). Page side margin on desktop.

space-9 · 120px

Large gaps between blocks inside a section. No longer section padding: at 120px most sections did not fit one laptop screen.

Shape

Radius and shadow

Shadows are for product images only.

radius-xs4px
radius-sm8px
radius-md12px
radius-lg16px

radius-pill999px

shadow-product

Product images only: screenshots and interface fragments. Never on page sections, cards, buttons or panels.

shadow-product-lift

The front-most layer in a stacked product image, such as the phone in the hero.

Components

Components

Each preview is the component's own preview.html, rendered with these tokens.

BenefitSymbol

One symbol per benefit: a dark line icon on a white rounded tile, with a small coloured badge on its top-right corner that names the change.

Guidelines

Button

The site's calls to action, in three weights: primary for Schedule a Demo, secondary for the trial, and quiet for in-page links like "See how Forms works".

Guidelines

Cover

FeatureCard

The card used for the three value props and for each part in the "How studios run with ScheduLink" grid.

Guidelines

IllustrationParts

The building blocks of ProductIllustration, shown one by one so they can be reused in feature pages, part heroes and other visuals.

Guidelines

Logo

The ScheduLink wordmark and icon, in the variants the site uses. Files are stored in this design system, so pull them from here rather than from a Drive folder.

Guidelines

ProductIllustration

The approved homepage hero image: one calm card showing a studio's day across three parts, Photoshoots, Tasks and Photographers. Use this pattern, and the parts in IllustrationParts, for any product illustration on the site, so every visual looks like the same product.

Guidelines

ScreenshotFrame

How product screenshots appear on the site. They are fragments, not full app windows: one idea per shot, cropped tight, with no browser chrome.

Guidelines

SectionHeader

The eyebrow, heading and intro paragraph that opens every section of a page. Using it consistently is most of what makes a long marketing page feel designed rather than assembled.

Guidelines

TabIllustration

The picture beside each platform tab: an almost-true, simplified view of the real screen in ScheduLink, drawn in the site's style with fictional data. Approved examples: Photoshoot management (Picture Day), Task tracking (Student ID Cards), Photographer scheduling (the week of October 12), Client relationships (Lakeview Elementary School) and Email and form automation (Picture Day's emails and forms).

Guidelines
